minutes.headline: Commission voted to name the beach house for longtime beach manager Genevie Nass and authorized the chair to sign the skate park right-of-entry agreement.
minutes.summary: The Parks Commission heard facilities updates, named the town beach house in memory of a longtime beach employee, and authorized signing the skate park right-of-entry license agreement. It also rescinded the earlier skate park construction end-date vote, to be revisited by October, reviewed the Marshall Park design and construction timeline and grant results, and scheduled a July 16 meeting to consider volunteers for the vacancy. A remote meeting on Monday July 1 at 2:30 was set to vote on a municipal employee beach rate.

attendees.role: parks staff/department head giving facilities updates

public_comment.stated_role: resident, local civil engineer, 105 Chesman Street
public_comment.topic: Offered to support the Marshall Park project as an interested citizen with civil engineering expertise.
Criticized town administration and the Select Board, not the commission, for delays in giving the skate park group access to the park.

votes.motion: Rename the beach house in memory of Genevie Nass as the Genevie Nass Memorial Beach House.
Authorize the chair to sign the right of Entry (license) agreement for the skate park.
Rescind the May 24, 2023 motion setting a skate park construction end date of June 30, 2024, and revisit the time period this fall (by October).
Approve minutes of April 24 and May 15.

budget_items.what_was_said: The trails grant was not awarded; the application had required listing a much larger set of projects.
An ADA grant application was submitted to cover the gap between first and second estimates; it is not a matching grant and is expected to be decided in the fall.
The dredging grant for Marshall Pond and the town beach was not awarded; the town may reapply.
One grant must be expended by a June 2025 deadline, and an extension may be requested depending on the construction schedule and November town meeting funding.
New local landscapers start July 1, and a priority list is being compiled for what can be afforded.
Proposal to charge town employees the residential rate at the town beach; to be voted at a specially posted meeting.

decisions.decision: Repurposing the T-ball field as a dog park was put back on the agenda for the next meeting pending the town manager's insurance review and the skate park construction.
Aim for a special meeting July 16 to consider volunteers for the vacancy, and the regular July meeting on July 31.
A fully remote special meeting set for Monday July 1 at 2:30 to vote on a municipal employee rate for the town beach, with public comment and a chair update.
Request to move public comment and board comment to the top of the agenda was raised.
A dedication ceremony for the beach house is to be planned for late July or early August, posted as a meeting.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted to name the town beach house in memory of a longtime beach employee; the minutes do not record the vote count.
The commission voted to authorize the chair to sign the right-of-entry license agreement for the skate park.
The commission rescinded its May 2023 vote setting a skate park construction end date, and will revisit the time period by October.
Three grant applications were reported: the trails grant and the dredging grant were not awarded, and an ADA grant decision is expected in the fall.
A fully remote special meeting was set for Monday July 1 to vote on a municipal employee rate for the town beach.

why_it_matters: Signing the license agreement and dropping the old end date clear the way for skate park construction at Marshall Park, but with no replacement deadline until the commission sets one.
Two grants were not awarded, so work such as dredging at Marshall Pond and the town beach, and trail improvements, has no outside funding from those sources for now.
A rate set for town employees at the beach would change what some residents pay for beach access.
watch_next: Remote special meeting Monday July 1 at 2:30 to vote on the municipal employee beach rate.
Special meeting aimed for July 16 on volunteers for the vacancy, then the regular meeting July 31, and a revisited skate park construction time period by October.
